why: The casting use case: one named character and a fair full of people who must be made up as the story needs them, partly by the world's own /recruit command. At least three new people, distinct and placed.
The same story without the world's own command: the /recruit turn is plain text, so anyone made comes from the game master asking the world author itself.
Casting switched off in the chat (the world author may not make anyone): the fair has nobody but the Marshal. Caught when the benchmark sees that nobody was made, as it must.

plant.what: the world author is switched off, so nobody can be cast
